fact_text: The IMF programme requires a primary budget surplus of about 2% of GDP, which the analyst called the most important IMF condition in the budget.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A proposal would cut the 29% corporate income tax by one point a year to 25% and phase the 10% super tax down to zero; the analyst saw these two cuts as the likeliest budget changes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On PKR 100 of pre-tax profit at a 39% combined rate, a 3-point cut lifts after-tax profit from about 61 to about 64, roughly 5% more.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimated a corporate tax cut could raise listed companies' fair values by roughly 5-7%, because markets price in the expected higher future profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A proposed zero capital gains tax on shares held three years or more was among the capital-market asks the analyst judged less likely to pass than the corporate tax cut.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A proposal would drop the tax deducted on dividends that one company pays to another, such as an operating company paying its holding company, which is deducted again at each step.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The petroleum levy on petrol and diesel averages about PKR 80 per litre, and its revenue target for the budget year was raised by about 20%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst doubted a 20% higher levy target could be met through volume, since fuel sales were expected to fall at high prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Unless oil prices fall quickly, the analyst expected the levy could be pushed toward PKR 90-100 per litre to hit the target, adding roughly PKR 10-15 to average fuel taxes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A climate finance levy on petrol and diesel is set to rise to PKR 5 per litre under an IMF climate finance facility condition, adding to the fuel tax increase.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A proposed extra fuel levy was framed to retire roughly PKR 1,000 billion of pending energy-sector dues over four to six years; the analyst said the IMF did not find the plan very significant.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Government dues owed to upstream producers would release cash to them if paid, and a fuel-levy-funded plan to clear those dues was discussed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An 18% sales tax on imported upgrade machinery would push a refinery upgrade from about 6 to over 7 billion; the analyst said a sales tax exemption, if the IMF agreed, could make refineries attractive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement cannot be imported economically because its value is low relative to its weight, so tariff-cut proposals barely affect domestic cement makers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Steel makers are protected by heavy import duties; if those duties are cut they may have to lower prices, so volumes could hold while margins shrink.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Steel imports from tax-exempt tribal areas were moved to a 10% sales tax, with a plan to rise about 2 points a year back to the 18% standard rate, which supports local steel makers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Provincial development spending, usually fully spent, drives more cement and steel demand than the federal PSDP, so provincial budgets matter more to these makers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst preferred cement makers with low bank debt and northern plants, since heavy borrowing leaves a company exposed if coal costs jump or government dues are delayed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expected budget measures might cut buying and selling taxes on property, which he saw as support for real estate and construction demand.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 1% capital value tax on overseas-held investments and the Islamabad capital value tax were both discussed for removal, to pull diaspora savings into Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Budget 2026 was expected to target about PKR 500 billion of new tax from services and provincially taxed agriculture, a smaller new-tax push than in earlier budgets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Duty and sales tax cuts on plug-in hybrids, EVs and battery vehicles were expected, and the analyst argued they could reduce petrol imports over time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower import duty and sales tax lower a car's price, which lifts volume under the government's car framework and so supports assemblers' profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When foreign exchange reserves come under pressure, the government can restrict or halt vehicle imports to save dollars, a risk to importers' volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Parts makers argue that new Chinese-brand entrants import parts instead of buying locally, and they seek duty protection to support localisation and jobs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A hybrid still burns roughly 60-70% of the petrol a conventional engine car uses, while a plug-in hybrid charged daily burns far less petrol.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said Indus Motor, which assembles Toyota vehicles, could bring plug-in hybrids to Pakistan if duty and sales tax on them are cut.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT exporters were taxed on 25% of export proceeds under a scheme due to expire, and the analyst expected an extension given government targets for IT exports.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Salaried IT staff pay roughly 25-30% income tax while direct freelance exporters pay less, which industry argues hinders building large software firms.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Goods exporters moved from a 1% fixed tax to normal taxation at 39%, with minimum tax raised to 2%; the analyst thought a return to 1% minimum tax likely, but a return to the fixed regime unlikely.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An extra 5% federal excise duty on urea and other fertilisers was under discussion with the IMF, which would make fertiliser bags costlier.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Urea makers have pricing power and can pass higher costs to farmers, so the analyst watched farm economics more closely than the budget for this sector.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima and FFC have lower gas costs than Engro Fertilizer, which lets them price their fertiliser bags lower.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Chemicals priced at import parity lose price when import duties fall, while bulky products like caustic soda and oxygen are shielded because they cannot be shipped economically.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst favoured chemical makers whose products are hard to import, naming Ittehad Chemicals, Sitara Chemicals, Ghani Chemicals and Pak Oxygen.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Annual electricity tariff increases were moved from July to January under an IMF understanding, so summer bills are not hit by a mid-year rise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Import duties on pharma raw materials keep declining under the IMF programme, and inputs still carrying duty were expected to reach zero, a modest margin support for drugmakers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule is that equities are forward-looking and often price in a development before it shows, while property prices can lag by six months to two years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Higher oil prices feed into inflation, which limits how far the policy rate can fall; the analyst saw a contained rate path as supportive for equities.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower oil prices or a settlement of the regional conflict could move Pakistan's current account from deficit toward surplus, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A global oil shock raises the chance that the IMF grants programme relaxations to countries hit hard, as Pakistan received during COVID.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Lose Money: 2026 Budget Moves for Every Investor' (YouTube transcript, undated)
